answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consider a river as the anchor of the cost.
